title: Tectonic Plate Movement with Time Control
prompt:
Create a single HTML file using Three.js that simulates tectonic plate movement on a flat world surface with time control. The scene is an educational visualization.

## Scene Setup
- Use a perspective camera at position (0, 40, 60) looking at origin.
- Add ambient light (intensity 0.5) and a directional light from (10, 30, 10) with intensity 0.8.
- Add OrbitControls for camera interaction.
- Sky background color: #1a1a2e.

## Tectonic Plates
- Create 4 flat rectangular box geometries representing tectonic plates on a flat plane:
  - Plate A (name='plateA'): size 20x1x15, color #8B4513 (brown), initial position (-12, 0, -8)
  - Plate B (name='plateB'): size 18x1x15, color #A0522D (sienna), initial position (12, 0, -8)
  - Plate C (name='plateC'): size 20x1x12, color #6B3A2A (dark brown), initial position (-12, 0, 10)
  - Plate D (name='plateD'): size 18x1x12, color #CD853F (peru), initial position (12, 0, 10)
- Each plate should have a subtle wireframe overlay to show grid lines.
- Add small colored markers (spheres, radius 0.5) on each plate to show movement: red on A, blue on B, green on C, yellow on D.

## Soldier Model (Scale Figure)
- Load 'soldier.glb' using GLTFLoader. Place the soldier model on top of Plate A at position (-12, 1, -8) as a scale reference figure to show how massive the plates are relative to a person. Scale the soldier to (2, 2, 2). Name the loaded mesh 'soldierModel'.

## Plate Movement Physics
- Plates move based on a simulation time measured in 'million years' (MY).
- Movement rates per MY (when simulation is running at 1x speed, 1 MY = 2 seconds real time):
  - Plate A: moves in direction (+0.15, 0, +0.05) per MY
  - Plate B: moves in direction (-0.1, 0, +0.08) per MY
  - Plate C: moves in direction (+0.1, 0, -0.12) per MY
  - Plate D: moves in direction (-0.12, 0, -0.06) per MY
- When plates A and B get within distance 2.0 of each other (measured center-to-center on X axis), trigger a 'convergent boundary' event: both plates stop X-movement and Plate A's Y position increases by 0.05 per MY (mountain building). Set state.convergentActive = true.
- The soldier model should move with Plate A (parent it to Plate A or update its position accordingly).

## Time Control UI
- Add an HTML overlay panel at the top of the screen with:
  - A 'Play/Pause' button (id='btnPlayPause') - toggles simulation. Starts paused.
  - A 'Speed' dropdown (id='selectSpeed') with options: 0.5x, 1x, 2x, 4x (default 1x)
  - A 'Reset' button (id='btnReset') - resets all plates to initial positions and time to 0
  - A time display (id='timeDisplay') showing 'Time: X.X MY'
  - A status display (id='statusDisplay') showing 'Paused' or 'Running'
- Style the panel with semi-transparent dark background, white text, padding.

## State Management
Expose window.__3D_STATE__ with:
- simulationTime: number (current MY, starts at 0)
- isPlaying: boolean (false initially)
- speed: number (1.0 initially)
- plateAPos: {x, y, z} - current position of plate A
- plateBPos: {x, y, z} - current position of plate B
- plateCPos: {x, y, z} - current position of plate C
- plateDPos: {x, y, z} - current position of plate D
- convergentActive: boolean (false initially)
- soldierLoaded: boolean (true when soldier.glb loaded)
- soldierPos: {x, y, z} - current soldier position
- plateCount: 4

Update __3D_STATE__ every frame.
physics_constraints: Plates move at defined constant velocities per million-year unit. When plates A and B converge (X-distance < 2.0), horizontal movement stops for both and vertical uplift begins on Plate A. All positions must remain NaN-free. Soldier position must track Plate A position.
